[1/3] Plan: build.py writes Harbor.apk.json next to the signed APK with version, versionCode, size, SHA-256 and build time; /android/Harbor.apk.json serves it; install page displays it; tests, README, ADR-026

impact_assessment.why: The APK download is a binary with no visible version or checksum, so a user cannot tell what they are installing or whether the bytes changed
impact_assessment.benefits: Verifiable sideload downloads; the page identifies the exact build; no server schema or runtime dependency
impact_assessment.risks: contract: one generated sidecar and a public JSON route; dependency: hashlib/json only; concurrency: metadata written after signing; state: one small file beside the APK
impact_assessment.mitigation: Generate metadata only after the signed APK is verified, serve it no-cache, show the full SHA-256, and test both present and missing sidecar cases

[1/2] Plan: app reads /android/Harbor.apk.json on launch, compares versionCode with the installed build, shows Update Harbor and opens the install page when newer; keep the existing Test/sync/share paths; rebuild, emulator-check, README/ADR-027

impact_assessment.why: The APK page now carries a version, but the installed app has no way to notice that the server has a newer build
impact_assessment.benefits: Users can see an update is available without manually comparing versions; reuses the public metadata route
impact_assessment.risks: contract: one public metadata read from the app; dependency: none; concurrency: launch-time background check only; state: none
impact_assessment.mitigation: Treat a missing or malformed sidecar as no update, compare integer versionCode, and only show the button when the served code is newer

[1/3] Plan: 192/512 PNG icons, manifest entries, /sw.js with root scope, network-first shell caching and API/media bypass, registration in index.html; service-worker and icon tests; Playwright registration dogfood; README/ADR-028

impact_assessment.why: Android users can install the APK, but the browser gallery itself cannot be installed to the home screen as a standalone app
impact_assessment.benefits: One-tap PWA install on Android/Chrome; cached shell opens offline; photos and API stay network-only and private
impact_assessment.risks: contract: public /sw.js, static icons and manifest; dependency: none; concurrency: service worker updates asynchronously; state: cache storage on the device
impact_assessment.mitigation: Serve /sw.js no-cache with Service-Worker-Allowed, use network-first so online clients see fresh assets, bypass /api, /media and /thumb, and delete old caches on activate

[1/4] Plan: DailyBackup records last run/copied/unchanged/bytes/error; ServerRunner attaches it to HarborApp; owner-only GET /api/backup; Sync tab Backup panel; tests, dogfood, ADR-029

impact_assessment.why: The daily mirror only reports into the Harbor window log; web users cannot see whether a backup is configured or when it last succeeded
impact_assessment.benefits: Backup state is visible wherever the gallery is open; no new storage or background thread; owner-only path
impact_assessment.risks: contract: one owner-only read endpoint and runner wiring; dependency: none; concurrency: status snapshot under a lock; state: status is in memory
impact_assessment.mitigation: Keep a small immutable status, update it after every mirror attempt, expose only to the owner, and show 'not configured' when no --backup-to was supplied
